notes: Maps the IEEE 1516.1-2025 §12.12.1.1 library-naming requirement to a C++ downstream package smoke test, not to a public-service TCK case. The focused check validates all three installed shared-library basenames and package metadata under 64-bit MinGW GCC 15.2 Debug. SISO-REF-080-2023 defines gcc12 for GCC 12 and later; Umbra now publishes gcc12 (source SISO-REF-080-2023), the 64-bit form without _32, the Debug d marker, and the Windows .dll extension. The GNU package smoke configure check rejects a divergent automatic GCC marker/source while allowing an explicitly user-configured marker. Applying SISO's compiler-family marker to MinGW is an implementation interpretation; the platform is separately distinguished by the Windows library extension. Evidence: CTest umbra_rti_package_library_nomenclature passed in out/mgw/shared/package-smoke-nomenclature-check-20261106. This is focused package-format evidence for this toolchain only, not cross-platform verification, third-party interoperability, or overall conformance.
